lesson.subject: maths
lesson.title: Place Value to 100
lesson.summary: Tens and ones, partitioning, the number line to 100, and comparing numbers.
learning_objectives: Know what the digits in a two-digit number mean
Partition numbers into tens and ones
Place numbers on a number line to 100
Compare and order numbers with < and >

standards.text: Recognise the place value of each digit in a two-digit number

success_criteria: I can say the tens and ones in a number to 100
I can show a number on a number line
I can compare two numbers using < and >
lesson.real_life: Counting pocket money, packs of pencils and pages in a book.

blocks.markdown:
Today's big question: how can we read big numbers like 47 and 83 quickly?

We will use tens and ones to find out.
blocks.say: Welcome back, number explorer! Today we have a big question. How can we read big numbers, like forty-seven and eighty-three, quickly? The secret is tens and ones. By the end, you will be able to tell what any number up to one hundred is made of, find it on a number line, and say which of two numbers is bigger. Let's go!

blocks.alt: Tens and ones make every number to 100.
blocks.caption: Tens and ones make every number to 100.

terms.meaning: The two parts of a number up to 100.

blocks.markdown:
Every two-digit number is made of **tens** and **ones**.

In 34 the 3 means 3 tens. The 4 means 4 **ones**.
blocks.say: Look at this number: thirty-four. Is it just one big lump? No! It is made of two parts. One part is tens. The other part is ones. A ten is a bundle of ten things, like ten sticks tied together. A one is a single thing on its own. Let's see thirty-four built from tens and ones.

scenes.caption: Here are 3 tens. Each blue stick is a ten.
scenes.say: First, the tens. Count the blue sticks with me. One ten, two tens, three tens. Each stick is a bundle of ten, so three sticks is thirty.

scenes.caption: And here are 4 ones. Each dot is one.
scenes.say: Now the ones. Each blue dot is just one. Count them: one, two, three, four. Four single ones.

scenes.caption: 3 tens and 4 ones make 34.
scenes.say: Put them together: thirty, and four more, makes thirty-four. So in thirty-four, the three is the tens, and the four is the ones. Tens first, then ones.

question.prompt: In the number 52, how many tens are there?
question.hint: The first digit is the tens.

blocks.markdown:
The digit on the left shows the tens. The digit on the right shows the ones.

The same digits in a different order make a different number!
blocks.say: Here is a secret. Where a digit sits matters. The digit on the left tells us the tens. The digit on the right tells us the ones. Look at forty-seven and seventy-four. They use the very same digits, a four and a seven. But they are different numbers! In forty-seven there are four tens. In seventy-four there are seven tens. Seven tens is much bigger.

blocks.alt: 47 and 74 use the same digits but are different numbers.
blocks.caption: 47 and 74 use the same digits but are different numbers.
blocks.say: Forty-seven and seventy-four. Same digits, different places, different numbers.

scenes.caption: 47: 4 tens and 7 ones.
scenes.say: Forty-seven. The four is on the left, so it means four tens. Four sticks, and seven dots.

scenes.caption: 74: 7 tens and 4 ones.
scenes.say: Now seventy-four. The seven is on the left, so it means seven tens. Seven sticks, and four dots. Same digits, but a different number!

question.hint: Which side are the tens on?
question.explanation: The 4 is on the left, so it means 4 tens.

points: A two-digit number is tens and ones
The left digit is the tens, the right digit is the ones
blocks.say: Let us remember. A two-digit number is made of tens and ones. The left digit is the tens. The right digit is the ones.

terms.meaning: Groups of ten. In 34 there are 3 tens.
Single things. In 34 there are 4 ones.
One of the number symbols 0 to 9.

mini_quiz.prompt: In 90 there are 9 tens and 0 ones.

blocks.markdown:
Counting in **tens** is quick: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50 and on to 100.

Each jump is one more ten.
blocks.say: Counting in tens is a speedy way to count. Instead of one, two, three, we jump by ten each time. Ten, twenty, thirty, forty, fifty. Each jump is one more ten. Say it with me, and keep going all the way to one hundred.

blocks.title: Count in tens
blocks.caption: Every jump of ten along the number line: 10, 20, 30 and on to 100.
blocks.say: Here is the number line. Look at the jumps of ten as we go along from zero to one hundred.

scenes.caption: One ten is 10.
scenes.say: Here is one stick. One stick is a ten. So we say: ten.

scenes.caption: Two tens is 20.
scenes.say: Add another stick. Now there are two tens. Count in tens: ten, twenty.

scenes.caption: Three tens is 30.
scenes.say: A third stick. Three tens. Ten, twenty, thirty.

scenes.caption: Four tens is 40.
scenes.say: A fourth stick. Four tens. Ten, twenty, thirty, forty.

scenes.caption: Five tens is 50.
scenes.say: And a fifth. Five tens is fifty! Every stick adds ten. You can count in tens all the way to one hundred.

question.prompt: Count in tens: 30, 40, 50, ... What comes next?

blocks.markdown: To **partition** a number means to split it into tens and ones. 36 is 30 and 6.
blocks.say: Now a big word: partition. It just means splitting a number into its tens and its ones. Take thirty-six. We can split it into thirty and six. Thirty is three tens. Six is six ones. Time for you to try it!

scenes.caption: This is 36.
scenes.say: Here is the number thirty-six. Let's split it into its tens and its ones.

scenes.caption: 3 tens make 30.
scenes.say: The three in thirty-six means three tens. Here are three sticks. That is thirty.

scenes.caption: 6 ones make 6. So 36 = 30 + 6.
scenes.say: The six means six ones. Six little dots. Thirty and six. So thirty-six is three tens and six ones!

blocks.title: Make 36
blocks.goal: Put 3 tens and 6 ones in the right boxes. Use the stars: each star is one. Move 10 stars to make a ten!
blocks.say: Here are twenty stars. Every star is one. Drag ten stars into the Tens box to make one ten. Do that three times. Then put six stars in the Ones box. That makes thirty-six!

blocks.title: Tens and ones at home
instructions: Make groups of 10 from your small things.
Make the number 24: 2 groups of ten and 4 on their own.
Make 31. How many groups of ten? How many ones?
blocks.say: Now try it for real at home. Find about twenty small things, like buttons. Make bundles of ten. Then make twenty-four, with two bundles of ten and four on their own. Then make thirty-one. How many bundles? How many ones?

question.prompt: What number is 4 tens and 9 ones?

blocks.prompt: Can 45 be made another way, like 3 tens and 15 ones?
blocks.answer_markdown: Yes! 3 tens is 30, and 15 more makes 45. But 4 tens and 5 ones is the easiest way.
blocks.say: Think about this. Could forty-five be made another way, like three tens and fifteen ones? Have a think, then tap to find out.

points: Partition means splitting into tens and ones
blocks.say: Remember. Partition means splitting a number into tens and ones. Thirty-six is thirty plus six.

terms.meaning: To split a number into tens and ones.
A word or symbol that tells us how many.

blocks.markdown: A **number line** shows numbers in order. Numbers get bigger as you go right.
blocks.say: A number line is like a ruler for numbers. The numbers sit in order, small ones on the left and big ones on the right. As you move to the right, the numbers get bigger. Let's use it to find a number.

scenes.caption: 65 is between 60 and 70.
scenes.say: Let's find sixty-five. First ask: which two tens is it between? Sixty-five is six tens and five ones. So it is past sixty, but not yet seventy.

scenes.caption: It is halfway, so it sits in the middle.
scenes.say: Five is halfway between zero and ten. So sixty-five is halfway between sixty and seventy. We put our star right in the middle!

question.explanation: 65 is 6 tens and 5 ones, so it is past 60 and before 70.

blocks.markdown: Play the game, then solve the detective puzzle: a number is hiding between 40 and 50.
blocks.say: Warm up your memory first. Watch the lights, then copy the order. After that, be a number detective. Here is a clue: a mystery number is hiding between forty and fifty.

blocks.title: Number lights
blocks.goal: Watch the order, then copy it. It gets longer each time!
blocks.say: Watch the lights carefully, then copy them in the same order.

question.prompt: A number is halfway between 40 and 50. What is it?

points: Numbers go in order on a number line
Round numbers like 60 and 70 help us find the ones in between
blocks.say: Remember. Numbers go in order on a number line. Round numbers like sixty and seventy help us find the numbers in between.

terms.meaning: A line that shows numbers in order, with small numbers on the left.
In the middle between two things.
Someone who works out a puzzle by looking at clues.

blocks.markdown:
To compare two numbers, look at the **tens** first. The one with more tens is bigger.

If the tens match, look at the ones.
blocks.say: Which is bigger, seventy-two or twenty-seven? They use the same two digits, so it can be tricky! Here is the trick. Always look at the tens first. The number with more tens is the bigger number. Only if the tens are the same do we look at the ones.

scenes.caption: 72 has 7 tens.
scenes.say: Seventy-two has seven tens. Here are seven blue sticks.

scenes.caption: 27 has only 2 tens.
scenes.say: Twenty-seven has only two tens. Just two green sticks. Seven sticks is far more than two sticks!

scenes.caption: So 72 is bigger than 27.
scenes.say: So seventy-two is bigger than twenty-seven. The tens decided it.

blocks.markdown: The signs: **greater than** is >, **less than** is <, and = means the same. The mouth eats the bigger number!
blocks.say: We have two special signs. Greater than looks like this, a mouth that opens towards the bigger number. Less than is the other way round. And the equals sign means exactly the same. Think of the mouth as hungry: it always wants to eat the bigger number!

question.explanation: 65 has 6 tens and 56 has 5 tens, so 56 < 65.

blocks.markdown:
A shop puts 10 pencils in each pack. Ali has 3 packs and 8 loose pencils.

He needs 40. We use tens and ones to see how many more!
blocks.say: Let's use tens and ones in a shop. Pencils come in packs of ten. Ali has three packs and eight loose pencils. That is thirty, and eight more. He needs forty pencils for his class. Tens and ones will help us work out how many more he needs.

blocks.alt: 3 packs of ten and 8 loose pencils make 38.
blocks.caption: 3 packs of ten and 8 loose pencils make 38.
blocks.say: Three packs of ten, and eight loose ones. That makes thirty-eight.

question.prompt: Zara has 27 stickers. She needs 30. How many more stickers does she need?

blocks.markdown:
**Ordinal** numbers tell us the place: first, second, third, fourth.

When we **round** to the nearest ten, we pick the closest ten. 46 rounds to 50.
blocks.say: Two more ideas. Ordinal numbers tell us the place in a race: first, second, third, fourth. And rounding. When we round to the nearest ten, we pick the ten that is closest. Forty-six is just four away from fifty, but six away from forty. So forty-six rounds to fifty.

blocks.caption: First, second and third place.
blocks.say: First, second and third place in a race.

question.prompt: 46 rounded to the nearest ten is...

points: More tens means a bigger number
blocks.say: Remember. More tens means a bigger number. Use the less than and greater than signs to compare. And round to the nearest ten by picking the closest ten.

terms.meaning: A number that tells the place, like first or second.
To change a number to the nearest ten.
